pattern_rationale: The pharmacy system drops periodic flat files matching rx_export_*.csv. Reading the exports, deduplicating re-exported records across daily files (latest file wins), and translating to FHIR matches the file_drop_ingest pattern.

alternatives_considered.why_not: The system does not expose an HTTP API; it only produces nightly CSV drops.
Direct read-only SQL database access is not provided; data is only available via file drops.
The source system does not push event feeds (such as HL7 v2 messages) in real-time.

sync.detail: Nightly batch polling of configured folder for rx_export_*.csv files

field_map.transform: Format as string: 'pharmacy-csv-' + RX_NO, replacing any disallowed characters with '-'
Cast string to clean RxNorm code representation
Parse DD/MM/YYYY date format and convert to YYYY-MM-DD

resources.merge_rule: Latest export file wins by RX_NO; re-exported RX_NO records update/overwrite existing MedicationRequest resource.

risks: Unmapped or unexpected STAT codes in future exports will fail status mapping if not handled.
START_DT lacks time and timezone information, so authoredOn date reflects date-only precision.
Overlapping daily exports might arrive out of order if file timestamps or naming order is corrupted.
human_review_points: Confirm that STAT code mapping ('A' -> 'active', 'C' -> 'completed', 'S' -> 'stopped') matches all clinical status definitions in production.
Verify whether QTY string parsing reliably produces valid numeric quantities for all prescriptions.
Confirm file processing sequence and archive strategy after ingestion.
